analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 427-1237). The file is documentation only, and the visible lines are unchanged context. The patch excerpt's changed ranges (about 4592-4891 and later) fall outside the supplied text, so none of the changes could be examined directly. No code, configuration or control is altered in the supplied evidence.

The visible text describes cluster onboarding, Nemotron Super local binding, prefix cache, MTP, logprobs and the managed slot. Prefix-cache statements (lines 755-800 and 1146-1170) say reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope and is off without one. They also say durable SSD checkpoints are encrypted under the provider's cache root and advertise a capability. This is consistent with T-041's existing posture: scope is coordinator-authored, the SSD tier is encrypted, the TTL is bounded and SEC-035 is accepted. I found no widening of the TTL, no weakened scoping and no new at-rest field.

Media admission (lines 625-705) charges ingress and media memory before decode, applies size caps and returns 400 or 503 on overflow. This matches the existing DoS and plaintext mitigations. The text does not mention temporary files for video, so T-050 is not contradicted.

Logprobs entries (lines 868-903) are returned to the coordinator relay only, so no new disclosure path appears. The managed slot and cluster onboarding (lines 496-566) describe local-network and sudo link-script behavior. The sudo script is owner-only and runs interactively, so no new attack surface is evident from the prose.

Open questions: the patch shows only the cluster served-speed records (serving scope, tensorAssistant) and a tp-check --layer-stride option, and those hunks sit in lines I could not see. A reviewer with the full diff should confirm they remain documentation-only and do not describe changed trust boundaries. Because the truncated patch is not proof of absence, I set needs_deeper_review to false only on the basis that the supplied lines show no security-relevant change.
